semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Video interpolation, by definition, refers to the process of generating intermediate video frames between existing ones, which is distinctly different from any domain in the Given List.

parent_domains.justification: Video interpolation is often considered a subset of video synthesis since it involves creating new video frames.
Video interpolation can be considered under video generation as it deals with generating frames to produce a continuous video output.
Motion generation involves creating seamless motion, which can include interpolating between frames to create smooth transitions.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Video synthesis is the most closely related parent domain to video interpolation as it directly involves creating new visual content, similar to how interpolation creates new frames.

closest_child_domain.justification: There are no more specific domains than video interpolation in the Given List, so it is its own closest child domain.

sibling_domains.justification: Video generation is a sibling domain as it falls under the same category of creating video content from existing data.
Motion generation is a sibling since it involves generating visual motion, which is an integral part of video creation and interpolation.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Video generation is the closest sibling to video interpolation as both involve the creation and generation of video content, although video generation is broader in scope.

unrelated_domains.justification: Video learning focuses on the computational learning aspect rather than creating or manipulating video content.
Image compression deals with reducing the size of image data and is not related to video frame creation.
Video representation learning is about understanding and representing video data, which is not directly related to interpolation.
Video retrieval concerns finding and retrieving specific video data, not generating or manipulating frames.
Image synthesis pertains to creating still images and not video frames.
3D vision involves depth and three-dimensional processing, not necessarily related to 2D video interpolation.
Image processing involves manipulating still images rather than video sequences or frames.
Computer vision is a broad domain involving understanding images and videos, not solely frame interpolation.
3D animation focuses on creating animated content in a 3D space, distinct from 2D video interpolation.
Image matching involves comparing and finding similarities between images, unrelated to generating video frames.
3D processing generally refers to handling three-dimensional data, not involving interpolation of video frames.
Image generation pertains to producing still images, different from interpolating videos.
3D imaging is related to creating or visualizing three-dimensional images, separate from video frames.
Pixel-based reinforcement learning is a learning paradigm, not related to frame interpolation.
Computer graphics involve rendering and visual simulations, broader and not specific to interpolating video frames.
Object tracking is about following objects in video sequences, not about generating intermediate frames.
